title: Room-temperature inversionless diamond nitrogen-vacancy electronic spin maser
abstract: We propose a method to create a room-temperature maser operating at approximately 2.9~GHz frequency using an ensemble of negatively charged nitrogen-vacancy electronic spins (NV) in diamond, without requiring population inversion. Our method considers a DC magnetic field of a few milli-Tesla (mT) applied along the perpendicular direction of an ensemble of NV spins aligned along a common axis. This perpendicular magnetic-field creates superposition states of $|m_{\mathrm{s}}=-1\rangle$ and $|m_{\mathrm{s}}=+1\rangle$ of the NV spin's ground state triplet levels and thereby makes it possible to drive all three transitions in the NV spin ground state. We model the system by including optical pumping of the NV spins, near-resonant driving of two transitions, and coupling the third transition to a near-resonant microwave resonator. Numerical estimates using experimentally realizable parameters show that inversionless masing can be achieved inside the microwave resonator using our method. As an application, we show that the output intensity of an inversionless maser ($1.1\times10^{14}$ spins) can be used for magnetic field sensing with a DC sensitivity on the order of a hundred pT/$\sqrt{\mathrm{Hz}}$. Our study opens a new direction in room-temperature diamond NV maser devices for quantum technological applications without the requirement of a strong bias magnetic field, as in conventional NV diamond masers.
summary: The paper details a theoretical model for an inversionless maser using NV spins in diamond at room temperature. By applying perpendicular magnetic fields and coupling the system to microwave resonators, they show that lasing can occur without population inversion. This technique enables highly sensitive magnetic field sensing with minimal external bias requirements.
main_problem: The authors propose a method to create a room-temperature maser using nitrogen-vacancy (NV) spins in diamond without requiring population inversion.
main_result: They demonstrate that inversionless masing can be achieved, leading to a magnetic field sensing sensitivity on the order of 100 pT/sqrt(Hz).
method: The analysis involves solving coupled differential equations for spin and cavity operators using quantum cumulants in the steady-state limit.
model_or_system: The system is an ensemble of NV spins in diamond, modeled by a seven-level structure driven optically, via near-resonant microwave (MW) and radio-frequency (RF) fields, and coupled to a microwave resonator.
key_observables: Photon number ($n_x$), spin polarization ($\langle\hat{\sigma}_{ii}angle$), second-order coherence function ($g^{(2)}(0)$), and magnetic field sensitivity ($\eta_B$).
important_parameters: DC magnetic field of a few mT, MW/RF driving frequencies (e.g., $\Omega_y/2\pi \approx 10$ MHz), and cooperativity $C$.
main_assumptions: The analysis uses weak correlation approximations and linear expansions in the small magnetic field deviation ($B_s$).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the schematic setup, energy level diagrams, numerical results for photon number vs. driving parameters, and sensitivity plots showing improvements with second-order treatments.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical model (seven-level system) to deriving equations of motion using quantum cumulants, solving these equations in the steady state, and finally analyzing the resulting magnetic field sensing performance by optimizing driving detunings.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it combines cavity QED principles with solid-state spin systems (NV centers), addressing open quantum system dynamics under strong coherent driving fields to achieve a practical quantum measurement device.

Spintronics.note: The core mechanism described—achieving lasing (coherent emission) using NV spins coupled to a microwave resonator in the context of magnetic field sensing—directly falls under the quantum-optics interface with spin systems, analogous to cavity QED/polaritonic lasing.

NV sensing of materials.note: The paper's main result is demonstrating highly sensitive magnetic field sensing ($\eta_B$) using NV spins in diamond, which directly aligns with the theme of spin-defect quantum impurities probing magnetic fields.
